source: AI Engineer Code Summit, San Francisco, 10–12 Nov 2026. Stills are single frames from the public YouTube recordings at 1080p (livestream Day 1 ZZ19zhYnDKY, Day 2 y9JtCCZP2MQ; standalone O_zcc6Xl12g). Quotes are verbatim from YouTube auto-captions (livestreams) or the AI Engineer automated transcript plus stream captions (standalone); auto-captions can mis-hear names (e.g. 'Graph Bot' for Grok Bot).
notes: Timecodes are the frame's position in the cited video, ±2 s (sections were cut at keyframes). The ?t= link starts 1–2 s earlier. views/likes only for standalone uploads (yt-dlp -j); livestream items have null. Frames are the broadcast program feed, so most include the event's layout (logo column, camera inset, lower third).

items.description: Wide shot of the main stage at the Hilton San Francisco Union Square: sponsor wall, 'AI Engineer Code Summit' logo, podium 'presented by Google DeepMind', the white AIE letters; Lauren Tan walks on for her talk.
items.slide_text: AI Engineer Code Summit (sponsor wall: Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS, Databricks, Devin, Factory, Sonar, Vercel and others)

items.speaker: Lauren Tan
items.description: Broadcast frame: Lauren Tan on stage (camera inset, facing the audience) beside her chart of Grok Bot team merged pull requests per month; lower third with talk title, name, 'Principal Engineer', SpaceX logo.
items.quote: last month our team shipped a ridiculous 11,000 pull requests to production, which is a wild number.
items.slide_text: grok bot team merged 11k PRs in oct · 23,370 total · jun 809 · jul 1,784 · aug 4,203 · sep 5,648 · oct 10,926 · @poteto

items.speaker: Lauren Tan
items.description: Broadcast frame: Lauren Tan (camera inset) with her 'revert rate' chart, share of commits reverted per month falling from 0.98% in June to 0.47% in October.
items.quote: the number of PRs that get reverted has actually gotten lower on a relative basis and is steady at about half a percent.
items.slide_text: revert rate · % of commits reverted · jun 0.98% · jul 0.61% · aug 0.47% · sep 0.48% · oct 0.47%

items.speaker: Zach Bruggeman
items.talk: How to build an agent that builds the culture
items.description: Broadcast frame: Zach Bruggeman (camera inset) with the slide '75% of all merged code at Ramp is written and shipped by Inspect' and a 10×10 grid with 75 squares filled; lower third with talk title, name, 'Principal Software Engineer', Ramp logo.
items.quote: Through this, we now see around 75% of all of Ramp's code being being written and shipped by Inspect.
items.slide_text: 75% of all merged code at Ramp is written and shipped by Inspect

items.speaker: Brian Kennedy
items.description: Full-frame stage shot: Brian Kennedy at the Code Summit podium in front of the sponsor wall and the AIE letters; lower third 'Your Judge Is Hallucinating Too · Brian Kennedy · Principal Engineer · zoominfo'.
items.quote: The agent doesn't even have a tool that can send an email. The agent made it up and the judge approved it.

items.speaker: Brian Kennedy
items.description: Broadcast frame: ZoomInfo's offline eval of its AI judge on 500 production steps: right 65% of the time, 118 bad steps accepted.
items.quote: it turned out the judge was right 65% of the time, so more or less a coin flip. It accepted 118 steps that it should have sent back. That's more than one in four of everything that it accepted.
items.slide_text: 500 PRODUCTION STEPS · THE JUDGE VS THE REFERENCE LABELS · THE JUDGE WAS RIGHT 65% OF THE TIME · BAD WORK IT ACCEPTED 118 MORE THAN 1 IN 4 OF ITS ACCEPTS · The most common miss: the report claims an action that no tool call performed.

items.speaker: Philipp Schmid
items.talk: I deleted 90% of my harness (And It Got Better)
items.description: Broadcast frame: Philipp Schmid (camera inset, facing the audience) with his title slide; lower third 'Member of the Technical Staff, Google DeepMind'.
items.quote: Models will keep eating the harness.
items.slide_text: AIE Code Summit · November 11, 2026 · I deleted 90% of my harness and it got better · Philipp Schmid · Google DeepMind · @_philschmid

items.speaker: Quinn Slack
items.talk: A Company Built Around the Agent
items.description: Broadcast frame: Quinn Slack at the podium (camera inset) with his title slide; lower third 'Quinn Slack · CEO · amp'.
items.quote: the new kind of companies that are two orders of magnitude smaller where everyone can do everything and where everyone has skin in the game

items.speaker: Quinn Slack
items.talk: A Company Built Around the Agent
items.description: Broadcast frame: Amp's headcount chart (log scale) staying at 21 people while 'the other guys' grow, with the timeline Jan 2025 Amp starts to 'Today: 21 co-founders'.
